clue.text: Adults have finished with these train times

parts.note: to school someone is to train or educate them
days can mean times or eras, as in 'in those days'

explanation.surface: A railway timetable that grown-ups no longer need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train times' reads as a railway timetable, but 'train' is a verb meaning to educate.
explanation.definitionFit: Years of education at school are behind every grown-up, so adults have completed them.

clue.text: Two drugs make one silly

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Taking a couple of narcotics turns a person foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or foolish person, someone silly.

clue.text: A car from East Germany, perhaps …

parts.note: Germany is an example of a nation state

explanation.surface: Asking whether a vehicle was made in East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage an estate is a car with a large boot and rear door (a station wagon).
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon, a type of automobile.

clue.text: … made to sound domestic

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word pronounced like the word made

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a car built to sound homely.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this clue's surface to 3-down's, but the two are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, the same role as a housemaid.

clue.text: Guardian's printers use this, perhaps too loosely

indicators.note: done loosely, the letters of the fodder are set free into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dig that the newspaper's typesetters scatter a punctuation mark around too freely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian's own name in 'Guardian's' needs this mark, so its printers must use it.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark showing possession, as in the 's of a possessive name.

clue.text: Operator means to connect with the Queen

parts.note: an engine is a means or instrument for achieving something
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A telephone operator's way of getting through to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs or operates machinery, especially an engine, is an engineer.

clue.text: Clear land

definitions.meaning: to ... a debt is to pay it off or clear it
to alight or come to rest, as a bird does

explanation.definitionFit: Settle covers both paying off what is owed and coming down to rest.

clue.text: A danger to traffic could be sinister

definitions.meaning: a curve in the road is a hazard for drivers
in heraldry a ... sinister is a diagonal band across a shield

explanation.definitionFit: A curve in the road threatens motorists, and the heraldic band is called a bend sinister.

clue.text: Crooked dealer's rough hard scrap

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is a crooked dealer

indicators.note: a rough version of something is unrefined and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest trader's coarse leftover metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat at card games, who deals the cards crookedly to win.

clue.text: Female who's particular about English

indicators.note: one word sits about another, so it wraps round it

parts.note: a nice distinction is a particular, fussy one

explanation.surface: A woman who is choosy where English is concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, a sibling's daughter.

clue.text: Place to grow fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: Somewhere to cultivate fruit or a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is ground planted with fruit trees.

clue.text: Gone to heaven instead, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a different possible version, here a rearrangement of letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone went to heaven in someone else's place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sainted has been canonised, received into heaven as a saint.

clue.text: Oversight! Right out of cultured pearls

indicators.note: cultured pearls are artificially grown, hinting the remaining letters are reworked
the letter for right is taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Admitting a mistake in leaving the correct cultured pearls out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or moment of carelessness, much like an oversight.

clue.text: A meeting of yes-men

parts.note: a gathering of people who all say yes is, read differently, a meeting of minds where all concur

explanation.definitionFit: When people all say yes they are in concord, a meeting of minds.

clue.text: Hormone causing Diane renal upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A hormone surge caused by Diane's kidney trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands in stress.

clue.text: Each trial is a turn-up for them

definitions.text: Each trial is a turn-up for them

parts.words: Each trial is a turn-up for them
parts.note: for those who try out new aircraft, every test means a performance or turn up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: People who fly new aircraft to try them out take each trial up into the sky.

clue.text: They're put on for a dry run

definitions.text: They're put on for a dry run

parts.words: They're put on for a dry run
parts.note: a dry run sounds like a rehearsal, but here means jogging without getting sweaty

explanation.definitionFit: Deodorant products applied to stop sweating, so a jogger stays dry.

clue.text: Something superior; it's found in convent

indicators.note: one word is found inside another

parts.note: a priory is a religious house, such as a convent
the word it, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Something excellent is discovered inside a nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given priority ranks above other things, taking precedence.

clue.text: Computer systems show Labour in the toils

parts.note: toils are nets or snares, as in 'caught in the toils'
labour means work

explanation.surface: IT systems reveal the Labour party struggling in hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toils' looks like hard work, but in the toils means trapped in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked groups of computers are called networks.

clue.text: One in prison, for example, shows feeling

parts.note: a prison term is one kind of sentence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel or perceive.

clue.text: Amount cunningly concealed in Exchequer

parts.note: the Roman numerals X and C sit at the start of the word Exchequer, and XC is a number

explanation.surface: A sum of money craftily hidden within the national Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exchequer is Britain's Treasury. Its letters 2-3 are XC, the Roman numeral, which the solver must then spell out as a number in words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, a quantity or amount.

clue.text: Supply shelter

definitions.meaning: to ... money is to supply or provide it
to put someone up is to give them lodging

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both providing funds and giving someone a bed.

clue.text: Left a line entry to the Web

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Going online through a single line.
explanation.definitionFit: A web portal is a site serving as a gateway into the internet.

clue.text: Catholic leader of men

definitions.meaning: catholic in lower case means universal or wide-ranging

explanation.definitionFit: General means universal, the old sense of catholic, and is also an army commander.

clue.text: An umbrella of character

definitions.meaning: an old British word for a large umbrella
Sarah ... is a character in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit

explanation.walkthrough: The umbrella sense comes from Mrs Gamp, who carried one in the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamp is a bulky umbrella, named after the Dickens nurse Sarah Gamp.

clue.text: This cooking instruction could be bipolar

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe step that has mood swings.
explanation.definitionFit: To parboil is to boil partly, a common step in recipes.

clue.text: Piece to hand over to uncle

definitions.meaning: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' as pawnbroker is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece, and also the act of leaving goods with a pawnbroker for a loan.

clue.text: Spot the first piece of music

parts.note: a mote is a speck or tiny spot of dust

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Identify the opening section of a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, a piece of sacred music.

clue.text: On course here for game

definitions.meaning: ... in Suffolk is a famous English racecourse

explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk racing town and the card game share this name.
